result:
I verified every claimed correction directly against the frozen files rather than taking the summary at face value.

## Score: 9.4 / 10

## Verification of the corrections (all confirmed)

| My prior finding | Status | Evidence I checked |
|---|---|---|
| Missing changeset / release notes | Fixed | `.changeset/directional-security-profiles.md` (minor, discloses the SDK block); `release-notes.md:16-22` Unreleased entry with an explicit **Release dependency** paragraph. `package.json:4` still `7.2.0` — no manual bump. |
| Unverified tree | Fixed | `/tmp/directional-full-tests.log:249-250` → 137 files / 2087 tests passed; `/tmp/directional-built-tests.log` → 21/21 against the **built** CLI via `AIRS_CLI_ENTRY`; `/tmp/directional-tsc.log` empty; `/tmp/directional-lint.log:95` 7 warnings, all `noNonNullAssertion` in the unrelated `runtime-commands.spec.ts`. |
| Absent direction silently created | Fixed, more strictly than I asked | `profile-policy.ts:107-110` refuses an absent direction; `allowMissingDirection` is passed `true` only for the clone-validated shared-only path (`profile-builder.ts:389`, `:409`), so omitted directions survive global edits. `management.ts:146` uses the default (false), so topic writes refuse too. |
| Exit-code inconsistency (1 vs 2) | Fixed | `ProfilePolicyError` (`profile-policy.ts:8`) → `common.ts:14` → `usageError`. Integration asserts `2` at `:283`, `:398`, `:430`, `:456/458`, `:496`. |
| Inactive legacy block escaped the revert guard | Fixed | `getProfileTopics(..., { includeInactive })` (`management.ts:223-246`); `topics-revert.ts:42-56` uses it **before** the PUT and delete; a retained legacy ref has `direction === undefined` so it trips the refusal. Covered at `topics-revert.spec.ts:67` and end-to-end at integration `:464-501`. |
| `malicious-code-detection` in directions | Fixed correctly | `buildAppProtection` (`profile-builder.ts:96`) uses `malicious-code` only when a direction is selected; `mergeSettings` (`:371`) defaults new blocks to `malicious-code`; legacy flag creation keeps the old spelling. `validateOverrides` (`:329`) injects a name only into the throwaway validation copy. |
| Empty flag-only directional create | Fixed | `profile-builder.ts:248-251` refuses it and points at `--config`. |
| Untested safety branches | Fixed | `management.spec.ts:1510` (location provenance + 4 active vs 5 including inactive), `:1533` (guardrail/topic severity preservation + duplicate identity refusal), `:1555` (absent direction + legacy refusals); `runtime-profiles.spec.ts:750` proves a directional omitted→null drift is caught, i.e. `canonicalPolicy`'s directional skip cannot erase it. |
| Library exports / readable output | Fixed | `src/index.ts:14-18` exports `PROFILE_DIRECTIONS`, `isDirectionalProfile`, `profileProtectionLocations`; `renderer/runtime.ts:146-152` adds a `Protection locations` row alongside the full policy. |
| Injected-default risk not stated in operator terms | Fixed | `profile-transfer.md:293-296` states that an injected per-direction default makes read-back and `--on-conflict verify` fail with already-created resources left in place, and that the fixture alone does not justify normalizing it. |

Unrequested hardening I also noticed: `selectAiProfile` (`profile-policy.ts:78`) no longer synthesizes an AI entry when `--ai-profile-index 0` is given explicitly against an empty policy.

The capability gate is demonstrably two-sided: `/tmp/directional-registry-capability.log` shows a clean registry-`0.34.0` install failing the assertion with the intended message, and `prepublishOnly` (`package.json:19`) runs it before `audit:prod` and `build`.

## Remaining findings (all minor)

1. **Trivial — empty direction block on a shared-only flag create.** `profiles create --name X --direction response --no-mask-data-in-storage` passes `hasAnyProtectionFlag`, so `profile-builder.ts:247-263` still emits `'content-type-configurations': { response: {} }`. The direction selector does nothing useful there. Defensible (it is an explicit opt-in to `per_content_type`, and the SDK schema permits empty direction objects), but the new guard doesn't cover this shape.
2. **Evidence nit — the passing half of the clean-install check isn't captured.** `/tmp/directional-clean-local-install.log` records only `added 2 packages`; the `check.mjs` success line is not in any log, unlike the registry refusal. The script at `/tmp/airs-directional-sdk/clean-local/check.mjs` is byte-identical to the registry one, so the claim is consistent, but the artifact asymmetry is worth noting since it is the one check that proves capability rather than refusal.
3. **Cosmetic — prose wrap.** `docs-site/docs/cli/runtime/profiles.md:48-49` breaks mid-sentence ("Selecting a direction on a legacy / update refuses; / use complete JSON…"). Renders fine as a paragraph.

No required implementation or acceptance work remains for the directional feature itself.

## Material limitations (distinguished from completeness)

**Permitted and disclosed release dependency (not a defect):** the SDK containing the directional schemas is unpublished. Tested artifact `/tmp/airs-directional-sdk/cdot65-prisma-airs-sdk-0.34.0.tgz`, sha256 `844aec52…a947df`; `package.json:64` and `pnpm-lock.yaml:170` keep registry `0.34.0` with a registry integrity hash and no override. Pinning the real published version, refreshing the lockfile, and re-running the capability check from a clean registry install remain outstanding by design, and `prepublishOnly` enforces that.

**Separate pre-existing release issue (not caused or worsened by this change):** Verdaccio implements no audit endpoint, and the public-registry fallback reports `sharp@0.35.4` / CVE-2026-96889 (`/tmp/directional-public-audit.log`). `sharp` is a direct dependency of the DLP test-file generator (`package.json:91`, range `^0.35.4`), untouched by these 42 modified files; since the range already admits the patched `0.35.5`, this is a lockfile refresh rather than a code change. It will block `prepublishOnly` via `audit:prod` independently of the directional work.

**Genuinely unverifiable here:** live directional service writes, live cross-tenant migration, and whether the service injects per-direction defaults — which, if it does, will fail read-back/verify exactly as the docs now state. Per-direction server-default allowances were deliberately not granted, which is the spec-mandated conservative choice.

**My own scope:** read-only review. I did not execute any test, build, or install; the check results above are my reading of the recorded logs plus direct source verification, and the snapshot SHA256 `c6b91d8a…9767c3` in the artifact is recorded, not recomputed by me.
